sources.entry: Machine Learning Crash Course: with TensorFlow APIs *(Google)*

summary.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
summary.one_liner: Google's practical, video-and-exercise introduction to machine learning covering regression, classification, data preparation, neural networks, embeddings, LLMs, and production ML.
takeaways: Covers regression and classification model fundamentals, including loss, gradient descent, and hyperparameter tuning
Explains working with numerical and categorical data, including one-hot encoding, feature hashing, mean encoding, and feature crosses
Introduces neural networks, embeddings, and an intro to large language models (new module)
Includes modules on production ML systems and auditing models for fairness
Modules are self-contained; beginners are recommended to follow the listed order
summary.summary: Google's Machine Learning Crash Course (MLCC) is a fast-paced introduction to machine learning that combines animated videos, interactive visualizations, and hands-on practice exercises. The course is organized into modules grouped under ML Models (linear regression, logistic regression, classification), Data (numerical, categorical, and dataset/generalization topics), Advanced ML models (neural networks, embeddings, and a new intro to LLMs), and Real-world ML (production systems and ML fairness). The page says it was refreshed to cover recent AI advances with more interactive learning, and that it has been used by millions since 2018. Each module is self-contained, so experienced learners can jump to specific topics.
